speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities. To better understand what you're dealing with, can you tell me how long this rash has been present and if you've noticed any changes in its appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration of five months without resolution suggests a chronic condition rather than an acute reaction. Do you notice any specific triggers, such as heat, sweating, or stress, that make the itching worse? Also, have you noticed any scaling, thickening of the skin, or small bumps on the rash?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since you have denied systemic symptoms like fever or joint pain, I need to determine if this is an allergic or autoimmune process. Do you have any personal or family history of atopy, such as eczema, asthma, or hay fever? Additionally, does the rash itch more intensely at night or when exposed to sunlight?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Urticaria. Based on the five-month duration of pruritic bilateral upper extremity rash without systemic symptoms or response to initial considerations of chronic dermatitis, this clinical picture is most consistent with chronic urticaria, potentially triggered by subtle physical stimuli or idiopathic causes.
